h: Stories, Stamina and a Country Park Next Door
p: What sets Hobbledown apart from a standard farm park is the storytelling. The whole place is built around its own made-up world and characters, so children aren't just walking from pen to pen, they're exploring a little land with its own legends. Younger kids especially tend to throw themselves into it, which is half the battle won for parents who want a stress-free day. Let them lead, follow the bits that grab them, and don't worry about seeing everything in a strict order.

Timing helps. Get there close to opening on a sunny Saturday and you'll have the play areas before they get properly busy. Bring a packed snack bag for when energy dips, because tired, hungry under-fives and a giant climbing frame are not a winning combination. A change of clothes really isn't optional if it's rained in the last few days. Plan on a good few hours; most families find that by mid-afternoon the little ones are happily worn out and ready for a quiet car journey home.

The setting is a big bonus. Hobbledown sits next to Horton Country Park, a large spread of fields, woodland and footpaths on the edge of Epsom, ideal for a dog walk or a calm stroll once the kids are flagging. Nonsuch Park, between Epsom and Cheam, is another lovely green space with plenty of room for a picnic and a kickabout. On Derby day in early summer the whole town is all about the racecourse, so if you're visiting around then, expect the roads to be busier than usual and plan your journey accordingly.
